items.title: Judge denies bid to restore 92 Tarrant County polling sites before midterms
items.summary: A judge denied a temporary injunction on Tuesday Oct 13, so the 92 Election Day polling sites cut by Tarrant County's Republican commissioners (316 in 2022 down to 224 for Nov 3; early-vote sites 50 to 47) will NOT be restored before early voting begins (Oct 19-30 in TX). Four Fort Worth residents — Councilmember Deborah Peoples, retired judges Maryellen Hicks and Kathleen Hicks, and ISD trustee Camille Rodriguez — filed suit Oct 2 alleging the cuts disproportionately burden Black and Hispanic voters (e.g., ZIP 76103 lost all its sites); county leaders defend the 3-2 Sept. 1 vote as cost savings (~$1M). The case moves to discovery, unlikely to change the map before November.

items.title: Spanberger touts record Virginia early voting: 450,000+ vs ~200,000 at same point in 2022
items.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, in a Scott MacFarlane (CBS) interview circulating Oct 13, said more than 450,000 Virginians had already voted — vs just over 200,000 at the same point in 2022 — calling it 'extraordinary voter turnout' across the state, including rural and historically Republican districts. Single-sourced (MeidasTouch Threads repost); Virginia is already the national early-vote leader this cycle. Spanberger's figure has not been independently verified against SoS data this run.
